newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ex-Fed chief Volcker worried about dollar - report.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Fed chief Volcker worried about dollar - report.

text.p: Former U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Paul Volcker said he was concerned about the strength of the dollar and the effect it may have on other countries, a Brazilian newspaper reported Friday.

The O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper said Volcker, who was visiting Sao Paulo, also warned that Brazil would have to be vigilant about its widening current account deficit and its dependence on foreign capital.
"The very strong dollar worries me. The United States can absorb this but other countries can't," Estado quoted Volcker as saying.
Brazil is due to announce Monday the current account deficit for July and foreign direct investment flows up to last month.
On Thursday, Central Bank Monetary Policy Director Francisco Lopes acknowledged the deficit could reach 5.0 percent of GDP in 1997.
But he also said the foreign reserves had risen to a record $63 billion, according to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable.
